step_goal: Define when HSConfig should lower guide-backed sequence claims into official `Combo.json`, choosing `>>` for same-turn lines and `>->` for cross-turn lines, while keeping vague synergy visible through suppression reporting instead of guessed runtime rows.
required_inputs: The official HearthRanger VisionAI combo syntax page and the shared JSON condition syntax page, pinned through the local docs cache manifest or live verification.
Exact deck identity with resolved deck-present CardIDs for every card that may appear in a combo row.
Normalized source claims that preserve `source_claim_ids`, the ordered card sequence, timing semantics, optional condition text, and whether the claim is an explicit sequence or only general synergy.
A combo contract field that separates concrete sequence candidates from vague support-package, setup, or payoff notes before runtime compilation.
A report-only suppression artifact so non-emittable combo claims stay visible instead of being silently dropped.
Package validation rules that check official row shape, segment parity, supported separators, and provenance outside the runtime row.
produced_outputs: A strict-JSON `Combo.json` only when at least one combo claim is concrete enough for official runtime syntax.
A `combo_suppression_report.json` that records every suppressed combo claim with raw claim text, resolved cards, suppression reason, and source references.
A combo contract or row-plan artifact that stores `rule_id`, ordered cards, timing kind, condition, segment values, and emission status before final lowering.
Per-row provenance outside the runtime row, such as `config_row_provenance.json`, linking each emitted combo row back to source claims and compiler decisions.
A validation report that proves strict JSON, official key shape, supported separators, and combo/value segment parity.
documented_capabilities: The official HearthRanger combo documentation defines `Combo.json` with top-level `GameCardId`, `ConfigComment`, and `ComboList.values` rows containing `comment`, `condition`, `combo`, and `value`.
The official combo documentation states that `>>` means a combo in one turn and `>->` means a combo between two turns.
The official combo documentation states that the number of card IDs in `combo` must match the number of value segments in `value`.
The official JSON config documentation defines reusable condition syntax such as `*`, `AND`, and `OR`, so combo rows may use documented condition expressions instead of free-text timing notes.

The local HSConfig design spec already states that the Combo compiler should emit concrete sequences, support both same-turn and cross-turn syntax, require at least two concrete CardIDs, and keep vague synergy report-only.
current_hsconfig_support: The current `compile_combo.py` already accepts both official separators, `>>` and `>->`, through an explicit `operator` field.
The current combo compiler already rejects invalid operators, sequences shorter than two cards, and combo/value segment-count mismatches.
The current `gameplan_contract.py` preserves card order from normalized combo claims and suppresses combos when referenced cards are not in the deck.

The current `gameplan_contract.py` defaults missing combo operators to `>>` and missing segment values to repeated `10` values, which means timing and scoring can still be compiler-filled instead of source-proven.

The current `surface_intent.py` exposes `Combo.json` as an optional surface when the contract contains combos, but it currently labels that intent as `same_turn_combo_sequences` instead of tracking same-turn and cross-turn separately.

The current `validate_package.py` checks only that combo rows have at least two segments and matching combo/value segment counts; it does not enforce the exact official combo row-key set and currently tolerates extra provenance keys inside runtime rows.
observed_gap: HSConfig does not yet require a first-class timing field that proves whether a sequence is same-turn or cross-turn before combo emission, so timing can still fall back to the compiler default `>>`.

HSConfig does not yet distinguish explicit ordered deck-present sequences from vague synergy strongly enough; today a claim with two deck cards and the word `combo` can become a runtime combo even when the guide never states the exact order or turn boundary.

The current suppression path is too narrow because it reliably suppresses `card_not_in_deck`, but it does not require suppression for missing timing, missing order, placeholder setup language, or unresolved generated-card assumptions.

The current runtime combo row shape carries internal provenance fields such as `source_rule_id`, `source_claim_ids`, and `confidence`, even though the official combo help page documents runtime rows only with `comment`, `condition`, `combo`, and `value`.
The current defaulting of operator and value segments risks overfitting because it can make a vague guide claim look like a concrete same-turn runtime sequence with made-up weights.
aggressive_generation_policy: Emit a `Combo.json` row only when the source-backed claim names at least two exact deck-present CardIDs, gives a fixed play order, and makes the sequence concrete enough to classify as same-turn or cross-turn.
Use `>>` only when the source or normalized claim explicitly indicates a one-turn chain, such as `this turn`, `same turn`, or an immediate follow-up sequence that does not span turns.

Use `>->` only when the source or normalized claim explicitly indicates a setup-then-payoff line across turns, such as `set up on one turn and cash in next turn`; never infer `>->` from mana cost, intuition, or general archetype knowledge alone.

Treat phrases such as `save for payoff`, `combo card`, `support piece`, `setup`, `pressure`, `tempo`, or `synergy with` as report-only unless a prior step has already resolved them into an ordered, deck-present sequence with explicit timing.
Allow combo-row conditions only when they are `*` or a documented JSON condition string; timing must not be smuggled into free-text comments.

Do not invent guide-specific strength numbers from vague prose. If segment values are not source-backed, use a deterministic compiler-owned default policy that is clearly marked in provenance rather than treated as guide-backed semantics.
Every suppressed combo claim must still be written to `combo_suppression_report.json` with enough detail for review, so conservative blocking does not erase useful sequence knowledge.
validation_gates: The research output JSON must cover every field in `fields.yaml` and pass `validate_json.py`.
Any emitted `Combo.json` must be strict JSON and must use only the official top-level keys `GameCardId`, `ConfigComment`, and `ComboList`.
Every emitted combo row must contain only the official runtime keys `comment`, `condition`, `combo`, and `value`; provenance must live in a sidecar artifact, not inside the runtime row.
Every emitted combo row must contain at least two concrete CardID segments, and the number of `combo` segments must equal the number of `value` segments.
Every emitted combo row must use only documented separators: `>>` for same-turn or `>->` for cross-turn.

Validation must fail if a combo row was emitted without explicit timing evidence, without explicit order, or with any card not present in the deck identity unless a separate generated-entity resolution step has already authorized it.

Validation must fail if a claim was routed to `Combo.json` even though its suppression reason is `missing_order`, `missing_timing`, `vague_synergy_only`, `card_not_in_deck`, or `generated_entity_unresolved`.
Validation must require a `combo_suppression_report.json` whenever source claims mention combo or sequencing but no safe runtime combo row is emitted.
recommended_design_change: Add a first-class combo sequence contract that stores `rule_id`, ordered `cards`, `timing_kind`, `operator`, `condition`, `values`, `source_claim_ids`, `confidence`, `deck_presence_status`, and `suppression_reason` before runtime lowering.

Tighten `gameplan_contract.py` so combo inference requires explicit sequence evidence instead of any claim that merely mentions `combo`; missing timing, missing order, vague synergy, and unresolved generated-card references should become suppression reasons rather than default `>>` rows.
Update `surface_intent.py` so combo intent distinguishes `same_turn_combo_sequences`, `cross_turn_combo_sequences`, and report-only suppressed combo claims instead of a single same-turn label.
Update `compile_combo.py` so runtime rows contain only the official combo keys and all provenance is written to sidecar artifacts such as `config_row_provenance.json`.
Strengthen `validate_package.py` and combo tests to enforce the exact official row-key shape, supported separator set, explicit timing provenance, and mandatory suppression reporting.
never_autogenerate_without: Official HearthRanger combo syntax documentation and official JSON-condition documentation pinned in the docs cache manifest or live-verified for the run.
At least two exact deck-present CardIDs for every emitted combo row.
An explicit ordered sequence with explicit same-turn or cross-turn timing semantics.
A documented `condition` string or the literal wildcard `*`.
Combo/value segment parity that passes package validation.
A suppression path for every combo or sequencing claim that cannot be lowered safely into official runtime syntax.
